original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Universal five-source, 31-output generic F2 connector at exactly two complete calls per source and output, adding the reverse transfer D:z1+=z0 to the one-way C:z0+=z1 alphabet. Determine the minimum restoring transfer count below the known eight-transfer endpoint.
scope_change_reason: Follow PR1615 open question 2 by changing the operation alphabet, not the source count. Both connector rows remain arbitrary dirty, every port-specific child and transfer is fully priced.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper complete connector loop could lower recursive interface cost; this abstract batch has no identified selected-supplier seam and cannot imply a paid-moment or kappa improvement.
stop_rule: First derive the complete optimistic bill and the two-root moving-frame reduction. Test restoring bidirectional loops at 2 and 4 transfers, then 6. Stop at a sharp attainable threshold or a complete below-eight obstruction. At most one pivot to a structural explanation; do not expand source count or claim a selected supplier.
evidence: Exact threshold6 in the enlarged bidirectional F2 alphabet. New78-call witness uses10 B+62 A+3 C+3 D; four sources switch physical ports. Moving-frame proof reduces the below6 decision to175 canonical word/partition pairs and2,102,100 four-transfer candidates. Two independent engines agree on full histograms, maximum31/32. Complete180-factor+6-pass free noncommutative replay,522 dense cases and semantic controls are registered. No paid supplier or kappa gain is inferred.
author: Adam Gall, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical derivation, exact experiments, verifier implementation, source review, and writing. No independent human review claimed.
optimistic_completed_budget: T=H+sum of the 10 complete B port prices+sum of the 62 complete A port prices+nC*sigmaC+nD*sigmaD. H includes admission/reservation of two dirty roots, preparation, routing/frame/head access not already inside calls, instruction construction/read/dispatch and final restoration. The known one-way endpoint costs72*c+8*sigma+H8 under equal port prices, while the old one-root repair costs74*c+H1. A t-pass candidate is favorable only when t*sigma+H-H1<2*c; no positive threshold is weakened.
success: A source-bound exact bidirectional witness below8, its sharp lower-bound proof in this incidence-minimal family, complete symbolic tariff and meaningful failure controls; alternatively an exact obstruction closing the proposed saving.
falsification: Reject any word with nonidentity dirty-root monodromy, nonrestored source injection columns, a readout dirt mismatch, a missing target mask, or uncharged port/transfer work. A cheaper root-call count alone is not supplier admission.
